SWE-POD
Evaluation pilot brief

Research question
How do repository ownership, delegation, and communication affect whether coding agents can deliver a change across deployed services?

Available demonstration
The Saleor Core and Dashboard customer-attributes scenario uses real repository snapshots, Git-enforced write access, CI and deployed services. The current grader reports feature completion, regressions and GraphQL agreement. The synthetic SeedCo environment adds seeded histories and released-client checks.

Proposed pilot
1. Reproduce the no-op and reference outcomes for a frozen task package.
2. Compare solo, fixed team, and fixed team with explicit chat disabled using the same model, tools, environment resources and budget policy.
3. Validate one new private scenario with a hidden deployment-level business check. Verify that a full reference change passes and each one-sided change misses the intended outcome.
4. Review deployment checkpoints, strict success, component scores, elapsed time, model cost and infrastructure failures.

Proposed delivery
Versioned task manifests, starting states, runner instructions, scoring output, and replayable sample traces. Broader training use can be evaluated on held-out task families at a matched inference budget.
